title: A reversible  N -acylhydrazone-based turn-on fluorescent probe for ultrasensitive detection of fluoride and cyanide in water, food, and oral-care products
content: A new N-acylhydrazone N′-(6-bromo-2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzylidene)-2,4-dihydroxybenzohydrazide (DHBH), was designed as a turn-on fluorescent sensor for the specific identification of F− and CN− ions. FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and LCMS analyzes were used to determine the molecular structure of DHBH. In its free state, DHBH showed modest fluorescence; however, the addition of F− or CN− resulted in a strong fluorescence amplification, which was ascribed to ion-induced modifications in the intramolecular hydrogen-bonding environment. In line with the improved DFT results, Job's plot technique determined a 1 : 1 binding stoichiometry for both anions. Further evidence of DHBH's preferred sensitivity to F− and CN− came from competitive-ion tests. Binding constants of 4.52 × 102 M−1 for F− and 7.79 × 102 M−1 for CN− were obtained from the related Benesi–Hildebrand analyses. DHBH showed low detection limits of 38.9 nM for F− and 38.6 nM for CN−, both significantly below the relevant WHO recommendation values for drinking water. Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) treatment of the DHBH–anion complexes confirmed the reversible sensing behaviour. F− was found in commercial toothpaste and mouthwash samples, demonstrating practical applicability, whereas CN− was found in apple seeds (Malus domestica), potatoes (Solanum tuberosum), and cassava (Manihot esculenta). HOMO–LUMO analyzes and solvent-dependent DFT computations shed more light on the electronic alterations connected to anion recognition. A DHBH-coated cotton-bud test kit was designed for quick fluorescent detection of F− and CN−. The fluorescence amplification of the test kit under UV exposure was investigated by RGB imaging using smartphone-based application and the R/G ratio served as a simple semi-quantitative indicator of the concentration of the analyte.
